rationale: Round 1 built, ran, and verified correct with no ICE fallback, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up across all seven passes while throttling only where NPB IS is genuinely sensitive: it is a hot-loop benchmark (rank/create_seq/full_verify dominate runtime) so RuntimeCost weights stay at or below 0.6, letting the selector skip heavy transformations on the hottest loop bodies while still applying them to cold functions like c_print_results; SUB gets the highest SecurityGain since instruction substitution is cheap, safe, and effective on arithmetic-heavy ranking code, and SPLIT keeps high Runtime/SizeCost weights (0.7) because it mainly enables FLA/BCF rather than adding direct cost; FLA and IBR are raised for strong control-flow concealment with moderate runtime throttling, BCF stays slightly below FLA since bogus branches are the worst runtime/coverage trade in hot loops, ICALL targets the modest call graph of this 7-function program, and IGV exploits is.c's heavy global-array usage (key arrays, verification flags); CorrectnessRisk weights stay low across the board so risk-favoring features do not drive selection, preserving the correctness that round 1 already achieved.
